objective: Creating more than one Increment in a Sprint and releasing before the Sprint Review
secondaryObjectives: Running a Sprint Review as a working session with stakeholders that can change the Product Backlog
Running a Sprint Retrospective that finds the most helpful improvements for the next Sprint
Deciding what happens to work that does not meet the Definition of Done when the Sprint ends
Engaging stakeholders and customers through the Sprint Review and the Product Owner without taking the plan from the Developers

brief.situation: You are the Scrum Master of the search team at Harbor Lane Outfitters, a fictional online outdoor-gear shop. Sprint 21 runs one week, Monday 1 March to Friday 5 March 2027, with the Sprint Review at 14:00 and the Retrospective at 15:30 on Friday. Sprint Goal: shoppers can filter search results by size and by what is in stock.
handover: Developers: Dev, Lena and Ana. Product Owner: Maya. Kim leads customer support and hears every search complaint.
Sprint Backlog: 16 points in four items. The team can release any Done item on its own.
howItWorks: The dashboard shows the commitments, the board, the burn-down, issues, the people and the events. Decisions come to you as the week unfolds; between them you can act from the action groups.
Move the week on when you are ready. Each morning the board shows what the Developers finished the day before.
On Friday you run the Sprint Review and the Retrospective, then write a short reflection.

reflection.question: Reflect on the Sprint: when value could reach shoppers, what happened to the item that was not Done, and how the Review and the Retrospective served their purpose.

parts.label: Increments and Done
parts.criteria: A Done Increment can be released before the Sprint Review, which is not a gate; only Done work is released or presented; the undone item returns to the Product Backlog and the Sprint keeps its length.
parts.modelAnswer: Filter by size met the Definition of Done on Wednesday, so we released it then: an Increment may be delivered before the end of the Sprint, and the Review is not a gate. The mobile chips failed the keyboard check, so they were not Done; we said so at the Review and returned the item to the Product Backlog. The Sprint kept its length.

parts.label: The Review and the Retrospective
parts.criteria: The Review as a working session where stakeholders inspect the Increment and the Product Backlog is adapted; the Retrospective picks the most helpful improvement, aimed at the cause, without blame.
parts.modelAnswer: At the Review the stakeholders used the filters, Kim brought what shoppers are saying, and Maya reordered the Product Backlog with them. The Retrospective chose one improvement aimed at the cause: run the accessibility check in the build on every change.

broken.headline: A working relationship broke
broken.body: Blame in a Retrospective, or a Review that ignores stakeholders, erodes the openness and respect that inspection depends on.

scoring.modelReasoning: Release a Done Increment as soon as it is valuable: several Increments may be created in a Sprint and delivered before its end, and the Review is never a gate to releasing value. Work that misses the Definition of Done is not released or presented; it returns to the Product Backlog and the Sprint keeps its fixed length. The Review is a working session in which stakeholders inspect the Increment and the Product Backlog is adapted; the Retrospective picks the most helpful improvement, aimed at the cause, without blame.
